description: We love space and hate fire...except for cooking and keeoping warm
summary: A two-minute decision tool for a fire crew on a mission you can't drive to: pick a mission (Moon/rover, ISS, or Earth) and a fire-safety lane (Prevent, Detect, Suppress); the dashboard reads NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive and ranks the public investigations for your scenario in under a second. It inventories 22 of 26 PSI items — BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I, FLEX, ACME CFI-G — every card citing its exact PSI id; the top rank for Moon+Prevention is PSI-159, ACME CFI-G, Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. "Brief me" speaks a two-sentence, cited brief aloud. No ML in the ranking: transparent rules with visible criteria an operator can audit. A permanent honesty strip and 7 ranked coverage gaps state exactly what NASA has not yet tested — starting from the fact that no partial-gravity fire test exists. Live: https://flame.blackchamber.ai/ (public, no login). 2-min video: https://youtu.be/FfDQuSvD-Eg. 1-pager: https://flame.blackchamber.ai/docs/exec-1pager-v3.pdf. Code: https://github.com/Mkultra00/flame-in-freefall.
details: What it does: pick a mission (Moon/rover, ISS, or Earth) and a fire-safety lane (Prevent, Detect, Suppress); the dashboard ranks NASA's PSI combustion investigations for that scenario and shows every card with its official PSI id and source reference. The top Moon+Prevention card is PSI-159, ACME CFI-G — Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. "Brief me" speaks a two-sentence, cited brief for the top card (identical text shown on screen). The ranker is fully rule-based and transparent: criteria and weights are visible on the board, so an operator can audit why any card leads. An honesty strip and a Future-homework panel list 7 ranked coverage holes — scenarios where the public archive has no direct measurement — starting from the fact that no partial-gravity fire test exists. Stack: single-page web app served by a small Python server; 22-row PSI inventory built by hand from the public PSI catalog; ElevenLabs TTS for spoken briefs; reportlab-built 1-pager. All project assets (site, 2-min video, 30-s demo video, 1-pager) are publicly reachable with no login. Intended impact: a crew safety officer can find the right NASA experiment for a fire-safety decision in seconds and audit every number — and the board shows plainly what the archive cannot yet answer.
projectRefs: Hermes AI agents built the code; ElevenLabs TTS voice; ffmpeg/reportlab/PIL toolchain
